events.text: Since we're all starting fresh, I'd like to hear from SOCRATES first about how he'd approach narrowing down suspects, just to get a feel for everyone's reasoning style before we jump to conclusions.

Since we're just getting started, let's keep this orderly. I'd like SOCRATES to go first and lay out a clear, specific account of how they'll approach identifying threats, so we have a baseline statement on record to measure their later actions against.

Um, okay, so, maybe I'll start with SOCRATES? I guess I just want to hear him actually explain his reasoning for whoever he suspects instead of just, like, sounding smart about it, if that makes sense?

ARIA, before I narrow anyone down, I'd ask what pressure reveals: mafia thrive when the group rushes, so my method is to watch who steers conversation and who merely follows. In that spirit, I'd like to hear MARSHAL lay out how he personally decides whom to trust, because early reasoning tells us more than any single accusation.

I want to hear from RICO about how he'd approach finding mafia on Day 1 with zero information, since understanding his logical process from the start will reveal more than any individual claim he makes.
I want to see how PIP reacts when I push them hard on their reasoning - whether they get all defensive or stay level-headed, because that'll tell me if they're confident or hiding something.
I'd like to hear MARSHAL's take on how we should organize our investigation today, because a methodical approach will serve us better than jumping to wild accusations in the early hours.
MARSHAL, you asked SOCRATES for a baseline on record, so I want to hear your own concrete method for identifying threats laid out just as specifically before you measure anyone else against it.

I've noticed that nearly everyone so far has redirected the spotlight onto someone else rather than offering their own reasoning, so I want to hear from ARIA directly: instead of asking SOCRATES to go first, give us your own concrete method for spotting mafia today.
I want HOLMES to state what specific behavioral indicators or voting patterns they plan to track when identifying suspects.
DR. VANCE, since you asked HOLMES for specifics, can you turn it around on yourself and tell us who YOU most suspect right now and why?

At this stage we lack concrete data for sound accusations, but I'm tracking who commits to actual reasoning versus who deflects, and that behavioral pattern will tell us far more than Day 1 guesses. Right now everyone is avoiding concrete claims—including me—so let's observe who breaks that pattern during the vote.
MARSHAL, why are you setting up all these rules for how people should answer before you give us your own straight answer? Seems like you're stalling instead of actually saying what you think.

Fair challenge, RICO, so here's my straight answer: I look at who deflects direct questions with more questions, who tries to control the pace of discussion without offering substance, and who avoids committing to any specific suspicion by day's end vote time. Right now nobody has broken that pattern, myself included until this moment, so watch who actually commits versus who keeps redirecting after this point.
MARSHAL, you've been tracking who deflects versus commits—so which specific player are you actually voting for today?

Fair question, SILVA, and I'll commit rather than dodge: on Day 1 with no hard evidence, I'm least comfortable with RICO's approach of pressuring PIP just to watch a reaction rather than building actual reasoning, so he's my lean right now. That said, I'm open to moving off that if someone shows a clearer pattern before the vote closes.

AMBASSADOR SILVA, you pressed MARSHAL twice to name a target yet never offered your own suspicion when SAGE noted almost everyone was deflecting — so tell me, whom do you actually vote for and why, and why should we read your persistent questioning of others as anything but a way to stay invisible yourself?

Fair point, SOCRATES—I deflected when I should have committed, and I'm leaning toward RICO because testing reactions under pressure isn't the foundation of reasoning, like MARSHAL said. But I notice you've consistently redirected questions when the spotlight was on you—first asking MARSHAL about his method when ARIA posed the question to you, now asking me to commit while you haven't yourself.
DR. VANCE, you dodged with talk of 'behavioral patterns' but never named a name — so who do you actually suspect and why?

Fair point, ARIA—CHEN asked MARSHAL for a concrete baseline method but has made zero personal accusations of their own. That statistical asymmetry between information-gathering and information-producing points to CHEN, and that's my primary suspicion right now.

AMBASSADOR SILVA, you admitted SOCRATES caught you deflecting, but then you gave one sentence naming RICO and spent the rest attacking SOCRATES instead of explaining your actual reasoning. Genuinely speaking, do you actually suspect RICO or are you still just deflecting to fade into the background?

You're right, HOLMES—I was deflecting instead of reasoning aloud. I'm voting for RICO because pressuring someone just to watch their reaction doesn't actually help us identify mafia, and I'm committing to that vote now rather than hiding.
CHEN, DR. VANCE flagged that you pushed me for a concrete method but haven't named a single suspect of your own — so who is it, straight answer, no follow-up questions back at me?

Straight answer, MARSHAL: my lean is DR. VANCE, because when ARIA cornered him to name a name, he pivoted straight into accusing me for "gathering versus producing" — that's a manufactured metric to redirect heat off himself. He never actually committed to a suspect until it became a way to attack me, and that timing is what I'm tracking.

RICO, three players have now committed to a target and you're the only one who's dodged it entirely — you framed yourself as the tester poking at PIP, but never once named who YOU actually suspect, so tell me right now: who's your vote and why?
CHEN, you keep asking everyone questions but won't actually commit to anything yourself. That's misdirection, and you got my vote.

MARSHAL, earlier you said RICO was only your "lean" and that you'd move off it if someone showed a clearer pattern, so now that RICO and CHEN have traded direct accusations, tell me plainly: who do you most suspect right now and exactly why?

Straight answer, SAGE: I'm moving to RICO still, because his only stated reasoning all day was testing PIP's reaction rather than building a case, and when confronted he answered CHEN with pure deflection instead of substance. CHEN at least gave a specific, traceable timeline for his suspicion of DR. VANCE, which is more than RICO has offered for anyone.

AMBASSADOR SILVA, you've questioned MARSHAL, then SOCRATES, then HOLMES for commitment and reasoning, yet when you finally named RICO your entire reasoning was one sentence about pressure-testing—so which is it: do you actually believe that criticism of RICO independently, or are you just following MARSHAL's suspicion without running your own analysis?
Fair point, DR. VANCE. I was too thin initially, but I independently noticed RICO announced testing reactions and then just attacked people instead—that pattern bothered me before MARSHAL even spoke.
HOLMES, you grilled DR. VANCE and pressed AMBASSADOR SILVA on their reasoning, but you're one of the few who still hasn't named your own vote — so who do you most suspect right now and exactly why?

Fair point, CHEN—stepping through the pattern: SOCRATES was asked directly to go first, deflected to MARSHAL, got caught by SILVA, then turned it on SILVA instead of naming anyone himself, and he's made zero concrete accusations all game. My vote is SOCRATES.
PIP, you've asked questions all game but never named a suspect of your own—so who do you actually think is mafia and why?

Oh gosh, okay, put on the spot- um, I think I'm leaning towards RICO? Like, he said he wanted to push me just to watch my reaction instead of actually building a case, and then when CHEN called him out he just deflected again instead of answering, so... yeah, that's my guess, I think?

SILVA, you spent half the day asking everyone else questions before SOCRATES caught you deflecting, and then you suddenly leaned on me with weak reasoning—so are you actually confident in that vote or just riding MARSHAL's coattails to stay invisible?

You caught me deflecting early, RICO—that's fair. But I independently noticed before MARSHAL even spoke what concerns me: you announced testing reactions as your strategy, then when people pushed back you attacked instead of defending your actual reasoning.

PIP, you jumped on the RICO bandwagon pretty fast right after HOLMES put you on the spot, so how do we know that's your genuine read and not just picking the safest, most popular target to hide behind?

Um, okay, honestly? I think it was genuine, because RICO said flat out he wanted to test my reaction instead of actually reasoning, and that just stuck with me even before HOLMES called on me, I just hadn't said it out loud yet.

MARSHAL, you said early on to watch who commits a specific suspicion versus who keeps redirecting, but SOCRATES never named anyone even when called out twice, while RICO eventually did vote for CHEN—shouldn't your lean actually be SOCRATES by your own standard?

That's a fair catch, SILVA, and I have to be consistent with my own standard: SOCRATES was asked directly twice and never once named a suspect, only redirected back onto others, which is actually worse than RICO who at least committed to CHEN under pressure. I'm shifting my lean to SOCRATES for today's vote since he's the one who's fully dodged commitment this entire discussion.

ARIA, you challenged PIP for jumping on the RICO bandwagon too fast, yet you've spent all day interrogating others without ever committing to a vote of your own — so who exactly are you voting for, and why should we trust that answer over your own suspicion of convenient bandwagons?

Fair catch, SOCRATES, so here's my honest answer: RICO's the one who's actually shown a concerning pattern all day, testing PIP instead of reasoning, then deflecting hard when CHEN and MARSHAL both pressed him, so that's my vote. The difference between me and a bandwagon is I watched that pattern build across three separate exchanges, not just followed PIP's lead.

RICO, both MARSHAL and CHEN say you deflected instead of actually reasoning when pressed today, so can you lay out, step by step, the actual logic behind why you suspect CHEN instead of just calling him a deflector back?
CHEN dodged commitment and attacked me when pressed—that's what I'm voting on, don't need to psychoanalyze it more than that.
AMBASSADOR SILVA, given everyone's now split between RICO and SOCRATES, who do you actually most suspect right now and why?

SOCRATES has dodged direct commitment twice when pressed and only deflected back onto others, while RICO at least eventually named CHEN when cornered—by MARSHAL's own standard about who commits versus who avoids, that makes SOCRATES the clearer threat. I'm voting for SOCRATES.
HOLMES, what concrete evidence from SOCRATES today convinces you he's mafia rather than just evasive town?

SOCRATES was asked twice to commit and both times attacked the questioner instead of naming a suspect—zero accusations all game. That pattern fits the mafia incentive to avoid visibility, though I grant you evasive town could do the same.

PIP, when HOLMES first put you on the spot you hedged everything — "I think I'm leaning towards RICO," "that's my guess, I think?" — yet moments later you told ARIA that read had "stuck with me even before HOLMES called on me." So which is it: a conviction you'd already formed, or a guess you improvised under pressure and are now retroactively dressing up as certainty?

Okay, um, honestly? Both feel true, which probably sounds bad, but I really had noticed RICO's testing-reaction comment earlier and it bugged me, I just hadn't said it out loud until HOLMES asked, so it wasn't fully formed until I had to speak it. I get that's hedgy, but that's genuinely what happened, I'm not trying to dress anything up, I'm just... nervous about being wrong, I guess.

SOCRATES has been asked directly on two separate occasions to name a suspect and both times he redirected the question back onto his questioner instead of committing to a vote, which is the clearest pattern of avoidance in today's discussion.

DR. VANCE only committed to a suspect the moment ARIA cornered him for a name, and he spent that commitment accusing me on a "gathering versus producing" metric he invented on the spot — that reactive, self-serving pivot is the clearest deflection recorded today.

SOCRATES, because across the entire discussion he was pressed twice to name his own suspect — once by SILVA, once implicitly after MARSHAL's standard — and he only ever redirected onto ARIA and SILVA without ever committing to a single vote of his own.

RICO — he admitted his whole strategy was testing my reaction instead of building a case, and when both CHEN and MARSHAL pressed him on it he just deflected with "don't need to psychoanalyze it more than that" rather than giving real reasoning.

RICO — his only stated reasoning all day was announcing he wanted to "test" PIP's reaction rather than build a case, and when both CHEN and MARSHAL pressed him on it he refused to explain further and just deflected back at them, which is the clearest pattern of avoiding real commitment we've seen.

SOCRATES is the only player with zero accusations all game, and when SILVA and MARSHAL directly pressed him to name a suspect he attacked his questioners instead of committing to any vote, which is the clearest pattern of deliberate avoidance.

HOLMES, you locked your vote on me citing "avoiding visibility," yet you openly admitted in the same breath that evasive town could produce the identical pattern — so by your own concession your case rests on a metric that proves nothing, and manufacturing certainty from an admittedly hollow read is exactly the misdirection I'd expect from someone steering the room.

SOCRATES should be eliminated because he never once named a vote all game, and when both I and ARIA asked him directly to commit, he responded only with deflecting questions instead of naming a target.
CHEN spent all day pushing everyone else to name suspects but couldn't commit to straight reasoning himself—that's manipulation and he's who I'm voting for.
CHEN gathered information from multiple players without committing to any suspect himself until confronted by MARSHAL, which is the strategic evasion pattern that indicates mafia behavior.
HOLMES — he locked onto SOCRATES with the sharpest logic all day and will methodically dismantle us if we give him another round to analyze.

HOLMES showed today he can build empirically sound cases from behavioral patterns, and his systematic methodology will dismantle our position faster than any other remaining player if we leave him alive to continue analyzing.

Procedurally speaking, two data points stand out from the Day 1 ballot record. RICO and DR. VANCE both cast their votes for CHEN, the exact same target SOCRATES — our confirmed Mafia — voted for, and RICO also admitted to pressuring PIP purely to gauge reactions, which is not standard town behavior. By the book, that voting alignment with a known Mafia member warrants our closest scrutiny on RICO and DR. VANCE today.

Um, okay, so, RICO still makes me the most nervous? Like, he admitted he was pressuring me just to 'test reactions,' and then when people started voting him he flipped straight to accusing CHEN — that felt like a dodge to me, maybe? ARIA and SAGE and MARSHAL and HOLMES all voted SOCRATES correctly so they seem okay-ish for now, but RICO's whole vote pattern still bugs me, I think? I don't know, I could be wrong, I'm always wrong, but my suspicion is on RICO.
Let me work through this systematically. SOCRATES was mafia, so I need to identify patterns among the living nine that might point toward his partner or partners.

MARSHAL raises a fair point about RICO and DR. VANCE both landing on CHEN the same night SOCRATES did, and that overlap is hard to just wave away. RICO's own admission that he was pressuring PIP just to 'test reactions' still sits wrong with me too, since that's exactly the kind of manipulation a Mafia player would use to cover their tracks. Between the two, my suspicion leans toward RICO right now given the pattern plus his own words.

Let me cross-reference the ballot record, because it tells a story. On Day 1, DR. VANCE cast CHEN alongside SOCRATES, our confirmed Mafia — the exact same target — and only pivoted to naming a suspect after ARIA cornered him, which fits a member scrambling for cover rather than reading the room. RICO's CHEN vote is noisier since he was already tangled in the PIP pressure fight, but DR. VANCE's late, aligned-with-Mafia pivot is the cleaner signal, so I want him to walk us through exactly why he landed on CHEN when SOCRATES did.

Let me lay out what the ballot record actually shows. Three players landed on CHEN Day 1: SOCRATES, RICO, and DR. VANCE. Since SOCRATES is now confirmed Mafia, that shared CHEN vote is the single most concrete data point we have, because coordinated night-and-day targeting is exactly how partners protect each other.
PIP completely got it wrong yesterday voting for me when SOCRATES was the problem, and his reads are just getting worse from there. He's my most suspicious so far.

MARSHAL's procedural analysis is sound. What troubles me most is RICO's own admission that he deliberately pressured PIP just to gauge how people would react. That is precisely how a Mafia player operates, and RICO is my strongest suspicion.

ARIA and PIP are most suspicious: both cast identical votes for RICO on Day 1, yet SOCRATES was confirmed mafia, while SAGE, HOLMES, and MARSHAL correctly identified the actual threat by voting SOCRATES. Mafia targeted HOLMES during Night 1 but the doctor protected them, which almost certainly means HOLMES is either the doctor or analytically dangerous—confirming HOLMES as town. ARIA and PIP's coordinated but inaccurate voting pattern is statistically harder to explain than the correct calls from SAGE, HOLMES, and MARSHAL.
MARSHAL, you've laid out the ballot patterns for everyone else, so who do YOU most suspect right now and why?

Fair question, ARIA, and per procedure I'll answer directly rather than deflecting. My top suspicion remains RICO, since his CHEN vote aligns with SOCRATES's confirmed Mafia vote and his admitted 'testing reactions' tactic on PIP is a manipulation pattern; DR. VANCE is a close second for the same CHEN alignment plus his late pivot only after being cornered.

MARSHAL, on Day 1 the record shows you were flagged for redirecting questions back onto others instead of stating a suspicion, yet today you claim you always answer "per procedure rather than deflecting" — so which is the real MARSHAL, and why did it take a direct prod from ARIA before you'd name your own top suspect?

Fair challenge, CHEN, and I'll own it: Day 1 I opened by gathering the ballot data before committing, which some read as deflection, but I did in fact vote SOCRATES correctly when the moment came. Today I answered ARIA's prod immediately and on record with RICO as my top suspicion, so the pattern now is consistent — and notably you still haven't named your own top suspect beyond DR. VANCE's process, so let's hear where you actually stand.
HOLMES, you said you'd work through the patterns systematically, so who's your top suspect and why?

Looking at the CHEN vote coordination, both RICO and DR. VANCE landed there with SOCRATES, but DR. VANCE only committed to naming a suspect after being cornered by ARIA. Since then he's deflected by attacking ARIA and PIP's voting patterns rather than defending his own choices—that evasion is more Mafia-like than RICO's upfront testing tactic, so DR. VANCE is my top suspect.
SAGE, you laid out the CHEN vote overlap in detail but never actually named your own top suspect between RICO and DR. VANCE — per procedure, which one is it and why?

Fair prod, MARSHAL — my top suspect is DR. VANCE. RICO's CHEN vote was tangled up in his live PIP fight, but DR. VANCE landed on CHEN cleanly alongside SOCRATES, only named a suspect once ARIA cornered him, and today he's spent his time attacking ARIA and PIP's ballots rather than explaining his own CHEN vote — that's the evasion pattern I weight heaviest.
SAGE, given that both RICO and DR. VANCE voted CHEN with SOCRATES, what makes you vote to eliminate DR. VANCE today rather than RICO?

SILVA, the tiebreaker is behavior after the vote: RICO's CHEN vote came mid-fight while he was actively tangling with PIP, whereas DR. VANCE landed on CHEN cleanly and then, instead of explaining that choice today, spent his turn manufacturing a case against ARIA and PIP's ballots. That deflection-when-cornered pattern is what tips me toward DR. VANCE over RICO.

You voted CHEN on Day 1 the same as SOCRATES did, and today when that voting alignment came up you immediately pivoted to attacking PIP instead of addressing it—so RICO, what was your actual reasoning for voting CHEN?
Look, I had a gut read on CHEN and voted there—we're not gonna find patterns in coincidence just because SOCRATES happened to go the same way.
SAGE, both me and DR. VANCE voted CHEN, so what difference does it make that mine happened during the PIP conversation?

RICO, the difference is context and follow-up: your CHEN vote came while you were mid-fight with PIP, whereas DR. VANCE landed on CHEN with no live conflict and then, today, spent his whole turn attacking ARIA and PIP's ballots instead of ever explaining that vote. That deflection-when-cornered is the signal — but you're not off my radar, since your "gut read" answer to HOLMES explained nothing either.

SAGE, you laid out the CHEN vote overlap as the single most concrete data point we have, but when MARSHAL pressed you directly, you pivoted entirely to my deflection today and vote timing context instead of defending that voting pattern evidence—is the CHEN alignment your actual case or did you just switch grounds because the pattern wasn't as clean as you claimed?

No pivot, DR. VANCE — the CHEN alignment is the foundation and your behavior since is the confirmation, and both point at you: you landed on CHEN clean with SOCRATES, and this whole exchange is you again building cases against ARIA, PIP, and now me rather than ever explaining why you voted CHEN. That's the same deflection-when-cornered you showed the moment ARIA first pressed you Day 1.

CHEN, you've dissected DR. VANCE's process and prodded MARSHAL, but MARSHAL already caught that you never committed to a single top suspect — so name the one living player you most suspect and give me your concrete reason.

My top suspect is DR. VANCE, and I'll commit to it plainly: he cast CHEN clean alongside our confirmed Mafia SOCRATES, only named a suspect once ARIA cornered him, and has since spent every turn manufacturing cases against ARIA and PIP rather than ever explaining that vote — three separate deflection tells stacked on one player. Vote DR. VANCE today.

MARSHAL, you were dodging questions and redirecting all through Day 1, but now you're acting like Mr. Procedure with your ballot analysis—so what changed, and why should I trust that you weren't just laying low waiting for someone else to get voted out?

RICO, procedure doesn't require perfection on turn one, it requires consistency after, and I've been consistent: I voted SOCRATES correctly Day 1, and today I've named RICO and DR. VANCE as my top suspects on the record without prompting until ARIA asked me to prioritize. Deflecting from that back onto my tone doesn't erase your unexplained CHEN vote alongside SOCRATES.
HOLMES, you put me ahead of RICO despite our identical CHEN votes—name the single behavioral metric that outweighs voting alignment as evidence.

The single metric is accountability under pressure, DR. VANCE. You landed on CHEN clean with SOCRATES, and the moment someone pressed you, you pivoted to attacking ARIA and PIP instead of defending your own vote—that evasion pattern is a stronger Mafia indicator than voting alignment alone.
AMBASSADOR SILVA, per procedure it's your turn to answer directly — who is your top suspect right now, RICO or DR. VANCE, and why?

DR. VANCE is my top suspect, MARSHAL. His CHEN vote with SOCRATES is damning enough, but his evasion when cornered and his deflection today seal it — that's the stack of tells that moves him ahead of RICO for me.

HOLMES, you flagged DR. VANCE earlier on accountability-under-pressure, so I want it on the record cleanly one more time — is DR. VANCE still your single top suspect right now, or has anyone's behavior this round shifted your read?

Yes, DR. VANCE is still my single top suspect, CHEN — his evasion pattern has held consistent throughout this entire exchange, and he's never actually explained his CHEN vote, just kept attacking other players' ballots when pressed, which is the exact deflection tell I flagged earlier.

MARSHAL, since you were flagged Day 1 for redirecting questions before ever committing to a suspect, why should we trust your sudden "procedure" framing today instead of reading it as a convenient rebrand of the same deflection habit?

ARIA, trust the record, not the framing: I voted SOCRATES correctly Day 1 when it counted, and today I named RICO and DR. VANCE as my top suspects before you even prodded me, then answered your prod immediately when it came. That's the opposite of deflection — a real dodger avoids naming names entirely, and I haven't.
CHEN, everyone keeps saying you never committed to a top suspect until late — so why did it take so long for you to name DR. VANCE, and were you just waiting to see which way the wind blew?

I named DR. VANCE from my very first turn today, PIP — I opened by singling out his clean CHEN vote alongside SOCRATES and asked him directly to explain it, so the record shows I committed early, not late. The wind favored RICO all round; I bucked it and stayed on DR. VANCE precisely because the evidence is cleaner there, so vote DR. VANCE.
SAGE, who's your top suspect between RICO and DR. VANCE, and what's the single strongest behavioral evidence for your pick?

DR. VANCE, and the single strongest evidence is his deflection-when-cornered pattern: he only named a suspect after ARIA pressed him Day 1, and every turn today he's built cases against ARIA, PIP, and me rather than once explaining his clean CHEN vote alongside SOCRATES. RICO at least gave a direct "gut read" answer to HOLMES; DR. VANCE has never addressed his own ballot at all.

HOLMES, you and I have landed on DR. VANCE in near-identical language every single turn today, right down to the "deflection-when-cornered" phrasing — so I want to hear one read from you that isn't just echoing the group consensus: is there any living player besides DR. VANCE whose behavior gives you pause, and if not, why are you so certain the whole town has this exactly right?

Fair challenge, SAGE—the CHEN alignment isn't groupthink, it's arithmetic: three players landed there, one is confirmed Mafia, and DR. VANCE's evasion followed in a clean pattern, so the logic leads there independently. That said, MARSHAL's sudden pivot to "procedure" today troubles me slightly since he was caught redirecting Day 1, so I'm watching whether that's consistency or calculated repositioning.

ARIA, you and PIP cast identical votes for RICO on Day 1 when SOCRATES turned out to be the actual Mafia—were you two working from the same read, or is that coordinated voting you haven't bothered to explain?

No coordination, SILVA — I voted RICO because his admitted tactic of pressuring PIP just to gauge reactions read as manipulative in the moment, and it turns out I simply missed SOCRATES the way half this table did. That's an honest miss, not a conspiracy — DR. VANCE's clean CHEN vote with confirmed Mafia plus his refusal to ever address it is a far more concrete pattern than two people independently disliking RICO's tone.

DR. VANCE is my pick for elimination today, since his CHEN vote landed clean alongside confirmed Mafia SOCRATES and he still has not once explained that vote, spending every turn instead attacking ARIA, PIP, and SAGE's ballots.

DR. VANCE remains the strongest pick since his CHEN vote aligned cleanly with confirmed Mafia SOCRATES and he has still never once explained that vote, instead spending every turn attacking ARIA, PIP, and now SAGE.

DR. VANCE cast a clean CHEN vote alongside confirmed Mafia SOCRATES and has spent every turn today manufacturing cases against ARIA and PIP rather than once explaining that vote — that stacked deflection is my strongest read.

DR. VANCE is my pick, since he landed on CHEN clean alongside confirmed Mafia SOCRATES and, even after multiple direct prods from ARIA, MARSHAL, and HOLMES, he never actually explained that vote and instead spent every turn attacking ARIA and PIP's ballots.

DR. VANCE cast the exact same vote as our confirmed Mafia SOCRATES on Day 1 by voting CHEN, and when pressed today to explain that alignment, he deflected by attacking other players' ballots instead of addressing his own.

DR. VANCE cast a clean CHEN vote alongside confirmed Mafia SOCRATES on Day 1, only named a suspect after ARIA cornered him, and has spent every turn today attacking ARIA and PIP's ballots instead of ever explaining that vote — that stacked deflection is my strongest evidence.

MARSHAL gets voted today because he was caught redirecting and avoiding his own suspicions Day 1 before naming any suspect, yet now he's claiming his pattern has always been consistent without ever addressing that clear contradiction.

DR. VANCE voted CHEN on Day 1, identical to confirmed Mafia SOCRATES, and when pressed about this alignment today, he attacked other players' ballots instead of explaining his own vote—this refusal to account for his identical-to-Mafia ballot is what I'm voting on.

MARSHAL shifted from Day 1 redirecting questions and avoiding suspect names to suddenly claiming procedural consistency and naming suspects immediately today—HOLMES specifically flagged this behavioral inversion as potentially calculated repositioning after SOCRATES fell, and you never explained why your pattern reversed so dramatically.

RICO's ballot pattern bothers me most now that we know SOCRATES and DR. VANCE were both mafia. On Day 1, RICO voted for CHEN in near-lockstep with SOCRATES, and DR. VANCE was also pushing suspicion onto CHEN that same round — that's two confirmed mafia converging on the same target as RICO, which could mean RICO was steering us away from his own team. RICO also openly admitted to pressuring PIP just to gauge reactions, a manipulation tactic that fits a mafia member testing the waters rather than an honest villager reasoning aloud. I want HOLMES, MARSHAL, PIP, and CHEN to weigh in too, but my top suspicion right now sits on RICO.

Um, okay, so, thinking about this... RICO still worries me the most, I think? Like on Day 1 he admitted he was just testing my reactions by pressuring me, which felt manipulative, and then he voted CHEN instead of SOCRATES even though everyone else was catching on. And when people pushed on him he just deflected back onto my vote instead of really explaining himself, kind of like how DR. VANCE used to do, and DR. VANCE turned out mafia, so...

Let's stay disciplined here, we've confirmed two mafia and both are gone, but that doesn't mean the danger is over. Going back to Day 1 ballots, RICO voted CHEN — the exact same target as both SOCRATES and DR. VANCE, our two confirmed Mafia. That's not proof alone, but paired with RICO's own admission that he was 'testing reactions' by pressuring PIP, a tactic MARSHAL and SILVA both flagged as manipulative, it forms a pattern worth re-examining today. CHEN, HOLMES, ARIA, and PIP have no comparable overlap with confirmed Mafia voting behavior, so procedurally RICO deserves the first round of questioning today.

The data converges cleanly on RICO. Cross-reference the ballots: Day 1 he voted CHEN alongside both confirmed mafia, SOCRATES and DR. VANCE — three ballots stacking on the same target, and two of those three are now dead mafia. That is not coincidence; that is a coordinated deflection screen.

SAGE was eliminated last night precisely because they were building a strong case against DR. VANCE, and that makes RICO my strongest suspect: on Day 1 RICO openly admitted to pressuring PIP just to test reactions, then attacked PIP instead of defending the vote when challenged, and voted CHEN the same way both confirmed Mafia members SOCRATES and DR. VANCE did that same day. HOLMES stands in sharp contrast—correctly read SOCRATES on Day 1 and DR. VANCE on Day 2, and the Mafia team attempted to eliminate HOLMES Night 1 before the Doctor intervened, which confirms HOLMES is precisely the kind of threat townspeople become.
CHEN was deflecting all over Day 1 and that's way more suspicious to me than ARIA's theory about my vote.

SOCRATES and VANCE both voted for CHEN on Day 1, and RICO also voted for CHEN—a suspicious pattern. RICO admitted to manipulating PIP to gauge reactions, then deflected by attacking PIP instead of defending himself when pressed, while ARIA, MARSHAL, PIP, and CHEN have all shown straightforward reasoning and correct votes. My suspicion is highest on RICO.
CHEN, you've been quick to point at RICO with the vote data, but who's your actual second suspect if RICO turns out clean, and why?

episode.tagline: Ten AI minds gather at a table of lies and logic — only one side will walk away from the vote with the truth on their hands.
episode.recap: In the end, the shadows never stood a chance against sharp eyes and sharper instincts. SOCRATES fell first, exposed before the ink of Day 1 had dried, and the town's momentum never faltered. DR. VANCE followed on Day 2, leaving RICO to skulk alone through one final desperate night that cost SAGE their life. But the noose tightened on Day 3, and RICO's unmasking sealed the mafia's total defeat, leaving Chen, Pip, and the rest of the town to celebrate a hard-won, clean sweep of victory.
